# Triage-quality fixture set (P2.3 / eval E07 groundwork)

`scenarios.jsonl` is a labelled `DeltaEvent` set for diagnosing
`orchestrator/score.py:score_threat_intel` against the scenario taxonomy
eval **E07** calls for (`.agents/evals/evals.md`). It is diagnostic
evidence for the `.agents/evals/orchestrator.md` / Phase 2 human checkpoint,
**not** a pass/fail gate: see `orchestrator/tests/test_triage_quality.py`,
which runs the scorer over this set and reports precision/recall without
asserting a threshold on either.

## Format

One JSON object per line (JSONL), UTF-8, no trailing commas. Each line is:

```json
{"event": <DeltaEvent-shaped dict>, "label": "staging" | "benign"}
```

- `event` is exactly the shape `orchestrator.state.DeltaEvent` accepts
  (`schema_version`, `event_id`, `kind`, `source`, `target`, `observed_at`,
  `fingerprint`, `attributes`). `DeltaEvent` is `extra="forbid"`, so `label`
  cannot live inside `event` — it is a sibling key in the wrapper object
  instead.
- `label` is ground truth for this fixture set only: `"staging"` means the
  scenario represents staging/attacker infrastructure that a human analyst
  would expect to be flagged; `"benign"` means routine, non-malicious
  infrastructure churn. It has no meaning to `DeltaEvent` or the graph —
  it exists purely for `test_triage_quality.py` to score predictions
  against.

## Scenario composition

30 "staging" scenarios (label `"staging"`), per PHASE2.md P2.3.1:

- `triage-staging-freshcert-*` (10): fresh cert + known-bad JARM —
  `attributes.recent_ct=True`, `attributes.known_bad=True`.
- `triage-staging-favicon-*` (10): watchlist favicon — distinctive
  `attributes.favicon_mmh3`, `attributes.known_bad=True`.
- `triage-staging-asnhop-*` (10): ASN hop — `attributes.shared_fingerprints`
  in `{2, 3}`, `attributes.recent_ct=True`.

70 "benign" scenarios (label `"benign"`):

- `triage-benign-cdn-*` (24): CDN rotation.
- `triage-benign-certrenew-*` (23): routine certificate renewal.
- `triage-benign-lbchurn-*` (23): load-balancer JARM churn.

All benign scenarios set `attributes.known_bad=False`, vary
`attributes.recent_ct` (mixed true/false across the set), and keep
`attributes.shared_fingerprints` at 0 or 1, plus scenario-flavored extra
attributes (`cdn_provider`, `cert_issuer`, `jarm`, `load_balancer_pool`,
etc.) that `score_threat_intel` does not read.

## Regenerating

The set was generated by a one-off, non-committed script (deterministic,
no randomness) that is not part of this repository. If the fixture set
needs to change, either hand-edit `scenarios.jsonl` directly or write a new
generator — do not assume one is checked in anywhere.

## Known result at generation time

With the current `score_threat_intel` heuristic and the `policy.yaml`
`mitigation_confidence` threshold of `0.8`, every "staging" scenario in
this set scores strictly below `0.8` (max observed: `0.75`, for the
fresh-cert + known-bad-JARM case) and every "benign" scenario scores at or
below `0.4`. That makes recall `0.0` against this fixture set and leaves
precision undefined (no positive predictions at all) — see
`orchestrator/tests/test_triage_quality.py` output / `last_run_results.json`
for the numbers from the most recent run. This is exactly the kind of
result the Phase 2 human checkpoint exists to review before anyone treats
`0.8` as a validated rather than merely plausible threshold.
